title: COD Extension Approved Without Delegation Authority
question: As of January 2026, what is the legal status of the Cimarron 2 COD extension, and what is the risk exposure if Conduit attempts to terminate under the sunset clause?

contributor.name: Sarah Lindqvist
contributor.title: Renewable Energy PPA Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Power purchase agreements, contract authority matrices, project milestone management, regulatory compliance

choices: The extension is likely enforceable against Conduit due to apparent authority and subsequent ratification (Dave's thumbs-up in January), but is procedurally deficient and creates audit risk; termination under the sunset clause would likely fail
The extension is void because Marcus lacked delegation authority; Conduit can terminate without penalty under the sunset clause effective June 30, 2027 (18 months from original COD)

The extension is valid — Marcus's email constitutes binding consent under the delegation matrix's email approval provision, and the 30-day wet signature requirement is an internal administrative matter

The extension status is indeterminate — the delegation matrix was violated, no amendment was executed, and SAP shows no record; Conduit should treat the original COD as controlling and issue a cure notice
